newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets fall.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets fall.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of April 30 were $21.496 billion, compared to $21.718 billion on April 25.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date fell to $12.429 billion from $12.433 billion the week before.
The central bank said the fall of $4.0 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $37 million.
--The purchase of $8.0 million from credit institutions, a product of the partial exercising of options on the sale of dollars to the central bank that were issued during the April 15 auction.
--Net income from operations by state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) worth $19 million.

--A net gain of $6.0 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between April 25 and April 30 the monetary base rose 4.403 billion pesos due to end of the month salary payments.
In the same period, the government's balance at the central bank rose 4.286 billion pesos, due mainly to tax collection.

The bank said it undertook monetary regulation operations for a total of 8.824 billion pesos in the same time frame in order to meet a greater demand for bills and coins as well as to overset the increase in federal governmetn deposits in the account it holds with the central bank.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
Apr 25 Apr 30
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $21.718 bln $21.496 bln
Monetary Base 73.555 77.958
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $12.433 bln $12.429 bln

*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
